(also: ⁧حَصَلَ عَلَى جَوَائِزَ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ ) · f) ⁧فِي شَارِعٍ أَكْبَرَ⁩ · g) ⁧فِي مَكَاتِبِ الوِزَارَةِ⁩ · h) ⁧مِنَ الصَّحْرَاءِ⁩ Exercise 7. a) ⁧مِنْ مِصْرَ⁩ · b) ⁧فِي مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ · c) ⁧مَعَ كَرِيمٍ⁩ · d) ⁧فِي المَدَارِسِ⁩ · e) ⁧مَعَ أَصْدِقَاءَ⁩ · f) ⁧فِي كُتُبٍ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ Exercise 8. a) In 1911, in al-Gamaliyya, one of the oldest districts of Cairo, between mosques and schools of Fatimid and Mamelucca era. b) Philosophy at the university; For many years he was employed by the state and wrote in the evening. c) A three-part novel that tells the life of a Cairo family between the two world wars; The titles of the three parts are names of real streets in old Cairo. d) In the cafés of Cairo, with friends writers and poets. e) The Nobel Prize for Literature in 1988: he was the first Arab writer to win it. f) ⁧شَوَارِعَ⁩ ( ⁧فَوَاعِل⁩ ; in the title is the subject, with a; in the second paragraph ⁧أَسْمَاءَ شَوَارِعَ حَقِيقِيَّةٍ⁩ : genitive with the a) · ⁧مَسَاجِدَ وَمَدَارِسَ⁩ ( ⁧مَفَاعِل⁩ ; genitive after ⁧بَيْنَ⁩ , with a) · ⁧مَقَاهِي القَاهِرَةِ⁩ (bad diptoto; in iḍāfa) · ⁧أَصْدِقَاءَ⁩ ( ⁧أَفْعِلَاء⁩ ; genitive with an indeterminate a) · ⁧الشُّعَرَاء⁩ ( ⁧فُعَلَاء⁩ , but with the article: kasra) · ⁧نُوبِل⁩ (foreign name: in ⁧جَائِزَةِ نُوبِلَ⁩ is the second term of theiḍāfa, genitive with the a). Warning: ⁧أَحْيَاء⁩ It's a normal plural, not a diptote. Exercise 9. 1. The summit was attended by Heads of State and Ministers from more than twenty countries. 2. The caravan arrived in a small desert village after a trip lasted a week. 3. The company moved from London to Dubai for tax reasons. 4. The writer received Arabic and international awards for her first novel. 5. The inhabitants of large capitals suffer from housing and transport problems. Reading with the endings: 1. ⁧رُؤَسَاءُ وَوُزَرَاءُ⁩ (name) · 2. ⁧فِي الصَّحْرَاءِ⁩ (Article: kasra) · 3. ⁧مِنْ لَنْدَنَ إِلَى دُبَيَّ⁩ (genitive with the a) · 4. ⁧عَلَى جَوَائِزَ⁩ (genitive with the a) · 5. ⁧سُكَّانُ العَوَاصِمِ⁩ (Article: kasra), ⁧مَشَاكِلِ السَّكَنِ⁩ ( iḍāfa: kasra).
⁧فِي الصَّيْفِ المَاضِي سَافَرْتُ مَعَ زُمَلَاءَ مِنَ العَمَلِ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ. بَدَأْنَا رِحْلَتَنَا فِي فَاسَ، حَيْثُ يَعِيشُ كَرِيمٌ، ثُمَّ⁩
⁧ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى مُرَّاكُشَ وَالدَّارِ البَيْضَاءِ. فِي فَاسَ مَشَيْنَا فِي شَوَارِعَ ضَيِّقَةٍ جِدًّا، وَجَلَسْنَا فِي مَقَاهٍ قَدِيمَةٍ مَعَ⁩
⁧أَصْدِقَاءَ لِكَرِيمٍ. وَفِي مُرَّاكُشَ رَأَيْنَا مَسَاجِدَ وَمَدَارِسَ جَمِيلَةً، وَاشْتَرَيْتُ سَجَّادَةً حَمْرَاءَ لِأُمِّي. وَأَخِيرًا وَصَلْنَا⁩
⁧إِلَى الدَّارِ البَيْضَاءِ، وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ أَكْبَرُ وَأَحْدَثُ. كَانَتْ رِحْلَةً رَائِعَةً، وَتَعَلَّمْتُ كَلِمَاتٍ مَغْرِبِيَّةً كَثِيرَةً.⁩

Exercise 11. a) It says miṣrin» e «ilā bārīsinwith the tanwīn. What aMiṣr» e «BārīsThey're diptotes: nothing tanwīn and genitive in a. Foreign or female cities and countries, names such as Aḥmad and ʿUmar, colors like aḥmar, plural as madāris and aṣdiqāʾ. They return to normal (kasra). No one can hear it in the daily talk, but in the official reading they do. b) Amman, Damascus and Baghdad. With a cameraman and a sound engineer on his channel. Young poets who write about their cities. In old cafes, narrow alleys and small bookstores (and in via al-Mutanabbī in Baghdad). Ramadan's first day. c) ⁧بَيْرُوتَ⁩ , ⁧بَغْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧إِسْطَنْبُولَ⁩ , ⁧تُونُسَ⁩ , ⁧مَكَّةَ⁩ : all with the a (genitive of the diptotes).
